newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Argentina telcoms rise on rate change.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Argentina telcoms rise on rate change.

text.p: Argentine telecommunications companies's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) surged on Friday because of a change in tariffs.
Telefonica de Argentina rose 1-3/8 to 30-1/2 in heavy trade of more than 1.5 million shares by midday. Telecom Argentina was up 2-1/4 to 47-3/8 on volume of 310,000 shares.
"Argentine telecoms are up for the most part from the rate rebalancing announcement," said Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities at UBS Securities.

The Argentine government set reductions in long-distance call rates and increased some tariffs for local calls, goals sought by the companies. Analysts expect their shares and ADRs to add to recent gains from earnings news because of the rate changes.

Shares in some other Latin American telecommunications companies rose, boosted in part by the Argentina rate changes and a rising U.S. Treasury 30-year bond. The long bond was up 25/32 to yield 6.81 and a rising bond meant more investors would look to put their money into Latin American equities.
Telefonos de Mexico was up 1/4 to 38-1/8 and Brazil's Telebras rose 3/4 to 87.

Among European ADRs and shares, Sweden's telecommunications supplier LM Ericsson rose one to 33-1/2 in heavy trade, boosted by general strength in the sector. Finland's Nokia Group was up 2-3/8 to 67-1/4.
Advances led declines 277 to 207 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 46.8 million shares by early afternoon.
